newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Bail appeal for Nigerians on treason charges.
newsitem.headline: Bail appeal for Nigerians on treason charges.

text.p: A Nigerian human rights lawyer on Thursday applied for bail for 11 dissidents detained since December and charged with treason after a series of bombings.

Radical lawyer Gani Fawehinmi, an ardent critic of the military government, told the court:"The police have only used speculative evidence to arrest and detain my clients, which is not allowed in Nigerian law.
"The strength of evidence against any accused persons, which in this case is weak, is important in granting bail. So, I will implore the court to grant the 11 bail."
Justice James Oduneye adjourned the hearing to Tuesday, adding: "Fawehinmi will conclude his argument on that day before lawyers for government will take their turn."
The 11 were charged last month with treason over a series of bomb blasts that rocked Lagos, killing three soldiers and wounding dozens.
Self-exiled Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka and two other leaders of the exiled-wing of the opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) group are also charged with the offence.
None of the accused were present in court.

Among those requesting bail is medical doctor Frederick Fasehun, chairman of the Campaign for Democracy (CD) pressure group. Twice this year another Lagos court had ordered his release but he remains in detention.
The security authorities maintain Fasehun was being held for the bombings, which Nigerian police have blamed on NADECO of which CD is a member. NADECO denies any involvement.
